concerns.text: The Bayesian Hierarchical model defines priors to 'decay with lead time' to reflect physics. However, the plan does not specify how the model handles the non-stationarity of weather events across seasons (e.g., winter vs. summer precipitation). Without a temporal covariate or seasonal blocking in the hierarchical structure, the model may conflate lead-time degradation with seasonal shifts, violating the construct validity of the 'physics-aware' claim.

The plan proposes a 'blocked/expanding window split' for Isotonic Regression but does not explicitly define the block size relative to the autocorrelation time of the forecast errors. If the block size is smaller than the effective autocorrelation length, the Diebold-Mariano test (FR-006) will suffer from inflated Type I error rates due to residual serial correlation, invalidating the statistical significance claims.

The fallback mechanism for the Bayesian model (reverting to Isotonic results on timeout) introduces a selection bias in the final reported metrics. If the Bayesian model fails specifically on difficult-to-calibrate cases (e.g., sparse events), the 'Bayesian' results will be a subset of easy cases, artificially inflating performance. The plan must specify a 'convergence-weighted' aggregation or a strict 'fail-fast' exclusion rather than a silent fallback to a different method.

The plan mentions 'minimum sample size (e.g., 100) per bin' for Isotonic Regression. For rare events (e.g., heavy precipitation at long lead times), this threshold may result in zero valid bins, causing the model to default to raw forecasts. The plan lacks a strategy for handling these 'zero-bin' scenarios in the statistical comparison (FR-006), potentially leading to undefined p-values or biased comparisons.
